messages:
sam_support: forwarding a customer report — they see embedding counts on invoice > dashboard for the month. customer pasted minimal repro and says counts jump after batch retries. cc billing

maya_billing: thanks — can you paste the exact sample request + invoice line they provided? need account id too.

sam_support: pasted below (redacted acct id):
> Customer payload (sent as CSV -> async batch):
> 
> POST /v1/embeddings/batch async
> Content-Type: application/json
> {
>   "account": "acct_REDACTED",
>   "inputs": [
>     "short text 1",
>     "very long text ... (truncated)",
>     "short text 2"
>   ],
>   "model": "open-embed-medium",
>   "batch_size": 128,
>   "retries": 3
> }
> 
> Invoice line: 12,432 embedding units billed, dashboard shows ~9,800 units.

eli_engineer: quick note — embeddings metering can differ if pairwise/rerank requests were sent, or if truncation produced different dim vectors (we meter by final computed vectors). Any chance customer also used rerank endpoint or client did pairwise locally?

sam_support: customer insists only used async embeddings. they did mention a small custom client that splits by newline. they pasted a log showing two retries for batch id b-9f2a. forwarding log: 
```
INFO batch_dispatch batch_id=b-9f2a size=128 attempt=1
ERROR upload failed status=502
INFO batch_dispatch batch_id=b-9f2a size=64 attempt=2 (client split halves after error)
INFO batch_dispatch batch_id=b-9f2a size=64 attempt=3
```

maya_billing: aha — looks like client changed batch size after a retry (128 -> 64) and sent the same inputs twice? That can double-count if our accounting treats retry as separate partial uploads. We usually dedupe by batch_id+sequence but if client re-splits we may not see matching sequence metadata.

jordan_devex: do we require stable batch metadata? I thought the async batch API expected the client to re-send the same batch_id and the same total_count. If they change internal splitting we can't correlate automatically. Shouldn't retries be idempotent though?

eli_engineer: idempotency is by request_id/batch_id for single upload. In this case the first upload failed halfway at the gateway and the client retried by splitting into two smaller uploads (no request_id on the parts). So server saw three uploads referencing same batch_id but different part_count headers: 1x full, 2x parts. Our metering path currently increments counts per successful vector ingest — we do a best-effort to dedupe using a small cache window keyed by (batch_id, total_items). If total_items differs we treat as separate. That explains invoice > dashboard.

sam_support: customer: "I didn't realize my client split on error. I thought we were idempotent."

maya_billing: can we reconcile? if we detect the pattern (one full + two partial with same batch_id within 5m) we could credit duplicates. Do we have logs to correlate?

eli_engineer: replay-bot ran a replay on b-9f2a and posted results — attaching snippet: 
```
replay-bot: replay results for batch b-9f2a 
  seen_uploads: 3 
  uploads: [full@00:12:21 size=128, partA@00:12:22 size=64, partB@00:12:22 size=64] 
  vectors_ingested: 256 
  unique_inputs_hash: 128
```

eli_engineer: vectors_ingested > unique_inputs_hash => double-count happened. The billing pipeline used vectors_ingested total. Dashboard query uses unique_inputs_hash for display. That mismatch explains the delta.

jordan_devex: proposed mitigation: (1) short-term credit back duplicate vectors for affected invoice lines when our replay shows unique_inputs_hash < vectors_ingested; (2) medium-term: change metering to prefer deduped unique_inputs_hash for billing conversation, or at least flag the invoice with duplication reason; (3) long-term: require part uploads to include sequence metadata that the metering service will use to dedupe.

maya_billing: for this customer we should credit the delta and notify. please list exact invoice lines + amounts so finance can create a credit note.

sam_support: will get amounts. also customer requested a quick doc update to warn about client-side splitting on retries. jordan, can you draft?

jordan_devex: yep — I'll add a short note to async-batch docs and a snippet recommending to preserve request_id and total_count on retries, and show example curl: 
```
# recommended headers on retry
X-Batch-Id: b-9f2a
X-Batch-Total-Items: 128
X-Batch-Sequence: 1/1 # or if part: 1/2,2/2
```

eli_engineer: additionally I'll add a small patch to metering: if we see same batch_id within a 10m window with differing totals, compute unique_inputs_hash and emit a duplicate_flag in invoice export so billing can reconcile automatically. Not immediate but ETA 3 days for a patch + tests.

maya_billing: sounds good. for now please create a credit for acct_REDACTED for the difference (invoice shows 12,432 billed, dashboard unique shows 9,816 => delta 2,616 units). I'll file a manual credit and loop legal if needed.

sam_support: told customer we're investigating and will credit if replay confirms duplication. they responded :
"Thanks — we found a bug in our client, appreciate the help. Please let us know when credit is issued."

eli_engineer: notes for records: root cause = client-side retry split without consistent part metadata => metering double-counted on ingest path. Responsible service: async-batch + metering exporter.

jordan_devex: follow-ups: add doc snippet, send template reply for support, add one-line billing FAQ entry.

maya_billing: I'll create credit ticket #CR-200501 and reference replay logs.

sam_support: closing loop with customer when credit issued. marking thread resolved for support. :white_check_mark:
